items.title: Parents ‘face difficulties’ with childhood vaccinations without familiar practice nurse
items.summary: Childhood vaccinations not done by the ‘familiar practice nurse’ are ‘making things difficult’ for parents, claims the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH).

items.title: Health visitors join calls for ban on AI ‘chatbot’ toys for children
items.summary: The government has been urged to prohibit the sale of toys with built-in AI chatbots to children until they are ‘independently proven safe’.

items.title: Exclusive: Future of community children’s nurses in Scotland at risk
items.summary: Scotland will have no specially trained community children’s nurses in 10 years’ time unless action is taken to secure the future pipeline, a nurse leader has warned.

items.title: Understanding bilirubin and newborn jaundice
items.summary: Neonatal jaundice is common, affecting around 60% of term infants and up to 80% of preterm babies. Although it usually resolves without treatment, it can sometimes indicate a serious underlying condition.

items.title: Sign up for audit to identify reasons for the postponement of children and young people's surgery
items.summary: NHS providers of children and young people's surgery in England are invited to join a GIRFT national audit of elective postponements at pre-operative assessment. Registration closes 23 December 2026.

items.title: PCRS webinar: health inequalities in asthma care for children, 30 November
items.summary: Primary Care Respiratory Society webinar for UK healthcare professionals on 30 November, 19:00 to 20:00, on asthma care inequalities, diagnosis and urgent to primary care working.

items.title: How this nursing team is making childhood vaccinations more accessible
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: Boost health visitors to reverse child vaccine decline, Lords urge
items.summary: A plan to boost the health visitor workforce in England is needed as part of a new national strategy to address declining rates of childhood vaccination, according to a new report from the House of Lords.

items.title: ViiV wins CHMP backing for paediatric HIV drugs
items.summary: CHMP has issued a positive opinion for ViiV Healthcare's paediatric HIV treatments, supporting expanded treatment access in Europe.

items.title: Practice nurse shortages undermining childhood vaccination efforts, Lords warn
items.summary: A shortage of nurses working in general practice means those among the workforce have less time to speak to parents about childhood vaccinations and is ultimately contributing to falling immunisation rates, a report has warned.

items.title: Rate of babies born with congenital anomalies in Wales falls
items.summary: The rate of babies born with congenital anomalies in Wales has steadily fallen over recent years, a new report has revealed.

items.title: iHV issues training guide for perinatal and infant mental health
items.summary: A new brochure to provide nurses, health visitors and other practitioners with specialist training information on perinatal and infant mental health has been launched by the Institute of Health Visiting (iHV).

items.title: Vulnerable children ‘forced to battle’ for adult social care support
items.summary: Children with complex needs transitioning into adult social care face worse outcomes due to workforce pressures, according to a report ordered by an influential group of MPs.

items.title: Primary care ‘lacks involvement’ in supporting transition from child to adult health care
items.summary: Primary care services are ‘not always sufficiently involved’ in the transition pathways to support children moving into adult services, a cross-party parliamentary committee has said.

items.title: Chickenpox vaccination catch-up campaign launched for children
items.summary: An NHS catch-up vaccination campaign offering protection against chickenpox to all children aged four to six years is being launched this week.

items.title: Plans to cut community nurses from children’s service dropped
items.summary: Proposals to cut community staff nurses from Suffolk’s Healthy Child Service have been revised by the county council following a public consultation. Suffolk’s Healthy Child Service currently covers health visiting, school nursing and support for young parents.

items.title: Skincare trends: how nurses can guide children and young people
items.summary: Given the physiological differences in the skin of children and young people compared to adults, elaborate multi-step skincare routines – which have become increasingly popular on social media – can risk damaging the skin barrier rather than protecting it.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of pH 5.5 hypochlorous acid in the management of complex wounds in paediatric patients
items.summary: This case series describes the benefits of using of a non-cytotoxic acidic pH cleansing solution in the treatment of complex wounds in paediatric patients, at two health centres in Santiago, Chile.

items.title: Deprivation worsens mental health in children with intellectual disabilities, study finds
items.summary: Children and young people with intellectual developmental disabilities (IDD) from disadvantaged backgrounds are more likely to experience mental health difficulties, according to new research led by University College London (UCL).
